chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Trio work and Wells restaurant in Harlem
summary: He had a trio at the Village Vanguard, played piano and organ at Wells where musicians ate after shows, and mentions other after-hours spots.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I think we got a little bit sidetracked here. Anyway, basically you're now into the Fifties, practically, and you're working with all kinds of trios and so forth. So I haven't much guidance here I can give you. For instance, how long...? Here they say with your own trio, long residences at Wells, Village Vanguard, Basin Street East, the Shalimar, Frank's Steak House...
I had a trio at the Village Vanguard with Jimmy Dutts(?) and a boy named Jackson on the guitar.
Jimmy Dutts(?) is a bass player.
Yes. I don't remember ...(? )...(? )... I also played... Of course, you're going to the Sixties.
Well, I was trying to stick with the Fifties first. When did you play at Wells?
When would it be that you played the organ at Wells?
I played both up there, piano and organ. Constantly. I mean, throughout the period that we're talking, the Forties... I played at Wells at various times.
What sort of place was Wells?
Wells was one of the main places where you could go after theatre, after a dance, to eat waffles and chicken, and have breakfast. It was open 24 hours a day.
It was a local...a very warm spot, right in the heart of Harlem. People came from all over. You had another spot ....(?)., too, named La Ma Cheri.

Those scenes were after hours. Billy Hicks was changed to another name later on... There were several places that you could go and eat until the wee hours of the morning. Creole Pete's was one of them...
